Colorado Cannabis & Hemp — Audit and Audited Final Report

Last audited: 1 November 2026. Research cut-off 1 November 2026. The 3 November 2026 general election had not taken place on this date, so no 2026 certified election result is reported anywhere in this file — including any Colorado ballot outcome. The federal baseline supplied with the commission was used as given and was not re-audited; only the report's statements of it, and Colorado's responses to it, were checked.

How the audit was done. A separate fact-checking pass, section by section, against primary sources only: Colorado Constitution Article XVIII §§14 and 16; Colorado Revised Statutes and bill pages on leg.colorado.gov; the Code of Colorado Regulations including 1 CCR 212-3 and the Colorado Register; the Marijuana Enforcement Division (MED) licence lists, enforcement and rules; Department of Revenue (DOR) marijuana sales and tax data; the Colorado Department of Public Health and Environment (CDPHE); the Colorado Department of Agriculture (CDA); the Office of Economic Development and International Trade (OEDIT); the Governor's executive orders and pardons; Secretary of State ballot and certified results; Colorado and federal court records; official tribal government sources; and official county, city and city-and-county sites and codes. Anything resting only on news, law-firm blogs, trade press or AI summaries is marked Unverified, not confirmed. Every claim carries exactly one verdict: Confirmed, Corrected, Removed or Unverified. Where a verdict counts a row as both Confirmed in part and Unverified in part, the counts below record the row under its dominant verdict and the table row itself states the split.

Cross-part resolutions applied once, everywhere

Separate checkers worked on different parts; where they differed, the assembly resolves the conflict once and the corrected text follows the resolution. Do not reintroduce the losing version.

  • Average Market Rate (bud): $648 is the Q1 2026 bud AMR (announced 10 December 2025, effective 1 January–31 March 2026), not a “December 2025 median wholesale” figure. Sequence used throughout: $1,721 Q1 2021 → $648 Q1 2026 → $607 Q2 2026 → $574 Q3 2026 → $601 Q4 2026. The Q4 2026 figure is confirmed from the DOR AMR page; the Q1 2021 figure is secondary-only and is labelled as such.
  • 488: 488 is retail stores reporting sales in June 2026, not cultivations. The 488-vs-478 “cultivation conflict” and any 791→488 calculation are removed. Cultivation series: 817 (June 2022, secondary) → 478 (MED 2025 report figure; verify against the report PDF itself).
  • MED 2,106: the 2,106 licence population is dated to February 2026 (Part 6), not end-2025. The MED press-release text states no total or breakdown, so the 2,106 total and all type/status breakdowns (687 retail stores, 478 retail cultivations, 210 manufacturers, 14 hospitality, 25,401 employees, 1,331 owners) are secondary reporting of the MED 2025 report — verify against the report PDF before citing as official. The MED PDF itself does not sum: headline 2,106 vs totals row 2,087 vs listed rows 2,071.
  • Hospitality counts: 14 (MED report) and 10 (February 2026 snapshot, Arvada/Aurora/Denver, from the HB 26-1117 final fiscal note) are kept as two dated figures, never averaged and never merged.
  • SB 26-007 “no smoking/vaping” detail: downgraded to Verify against the enrolled text. Enactment is confirmed (signed 30 March 2026, effective 12 August 2026), but the leg.colorado.gov summary does not contain the smoking/vaping detail, so the Parts 0–2 “Confirmed” is not carried forward.
  • SB 23-271 hemp age/ratio tests: Part 7 governs. The sales test in §25-5-427(8)(e) is OR (>1.25 mg OR ratio <20:1 = no sale under 21); the labelling trigger in 6 CCR 1010-24.7 is AND. Manufacture bans (Rule 24.9) and sales bans (§25-5-427(8)(f)–(g)) pair the serving counts differently and are stated separately. Do not conflate them.
  • Contaminant limits: Rule 4-215 in the current 1 CCR 212-3 numbering (effective 5 January 2026), not Rule 4-115. Rule 4-115 is the programme rule. Cornell reproductions lag the renumbering.
  • Denver taxes: the official Denver sheet effective 1 January 2025 governs — general 5.15%, retail total 26.75%, medical 9.15%. The 4.81% / 26.41% / 8.81% (2022) figures are superseded and removed.
  • Social equity eligibility: the current criteria are §44-10-308(6) (5-year tests, assistance programmes, narrowed arrest criteria, no residency/income test). The OEDIT 15-year/1980–2010 list is only the pre-1 February 2025 track (§44-10-308(4)). The secondary “1 April 2025” date is deleted; 1 February 2025 is confirmed.
  • HB 26-1117: DIED — postponed indefinitely 7 May 2026 (final fiscal note 8 June 2026). It is never cited as law, and its hospitality details are testimony, not statute.
  • HB 26-1409 local share: 10% → 3.5% from 1 July 2025 (SB 25-268, signed 3 June 2025) → 0% from 1 July 2026 (HB 26-1409, signed 4 June 2026). Whether 0% is permanent or FY2026–27 only remains Verify against the signed act (§39-28.8-203) — the reengrossed text suggests 3.5% may reappear 1 July 2027.
  • Part 8 headline stands: ZERO properties meet the strict verified standard on the evidence opened. 2490 West 2nd Avenue, Denver ($1,935,000, licence #403-00080 per listing snippets) is the closest candidate only — its full listing was not opened and the licence was not checked against MED.
  • Tribal “state-licensed” question: remains Verify throughout. No statement in this file treats a tribal medical programme as “state-licensed” under the federal rule, and no Colorado tribal medical programme was located.

Internal contradictions resolved (single figure adopted, as instructed):

  1. Bud price $648 vs $601: not a contradiction — $648 = Q1 2026 bud AMR; $601 = Q4 2026 bud AMR. The report's "December 2025" label for $648 is the error (it was announced 10 Dec 2025). Adopted sequence: $1,721 (Q1 2021) → $648 (Q1 2026) → $607 (Q2 2026, secondary-reported) → $574 (Q3 2026) → $601 (Q4 2026).
  2. Cultivation 478 vs 488: 488 is retail stores reporting sales (June 2026), not cultivations. Adopted cultivation figure: 478 (end 2025, MED report via secondary, Verify vs PDF).
  3. Hospitality 14 vs 10: 14 = end-2025 MED-report figure (Verify vs PDF); 10 = Feb 2026 fiscal-note count. Adopted latest: 10 (Feb 2026); both retained with dates, never averaged.
  4. Gifting 1 oz vs 2 oz: NOT resolved to 2 oz — adopted advice figure is 1 oz (constitutional text) with 2 oz kept Verify. Secondary summaries alone do not override the constitutional text.
  5. Sales peak DOR $2.23bn vs Headset $1.8bn: adopted DOR $2,228,994,553; Headset is a retailer sample only.
  6. BEST $40m vs 90%: both existed at different layers — constitutional floor $40m; HB 18-1070 enacted greater-of-$40m-or-90% from 1 July 2018; later recital indicates all-excise crediting from FY 2019-20 (except FY 2020-21). DOR's simplified "$40m/remainder" page is not the complete current rule. Exact current formula stays Verify.

Note: the DOR page describes the dataset as unaffiliated transfers for the median calculation — the original's "AMR generally for affiliated transfers" is the excise-application rule, not the dataset rule; the corrected text keeps both statements distinct.

7.1Hemp definition: Cannabis sativa L., any part, ≤0.3% delta-9 THC dry weight, tested for total THC through post-decarboxylationCorrectedhttps://colorado.public.law/statutes/crs_35-61-101 ; https://www.law.cornell.edu/regulations/colorado/title-8/agency-1203/division-23/part-1Statute §35-61-101(7): hemp = Cannabis sativa L. and any part, including seeds and all derivatives/extracts/cannabinoids/isomers/acids/salts, with delta-9 THC ≤0.3% dry weight. Operational compliance test in 8 CCR 1203-23 is total THC, and §35-61-101 defines “acceptable hemp THC level” by applying measurement of uncertainty so the range includes ≤0.3%. Total THC = (%THCA × 0.877) + %THC (6 CCR 1010-24.4, “Total THC”).

V §§2(b), (d), (g), (n), (p) and §2; applies to all hemp operations on Tribe's Lands incl. fee lands within/outside exterior boundaries; no cultivation/possession/distribution/transport/import without licence (through-transport not regulated if not unloaded); licences: Hemp Industry, Hemp Import, Hemp Cultivation, Hemp Distribution, Hemp Product Manufacturing, Hemp Transport (not required for through-transport not delivered/deposited); DOI code M45754, licences M45754_####; administered by Cannabis Regulatory Commission under Cannabis Control ActConfirmedUSDA PDF aboveRetained. 10.3 Ute Mountain — marijuana exclusionPlan Title I §1.07: Cannabis Control Act “allows issuance of various licenses related to hemp and does not authorize any licenses related to marijuana”; Act §1.04.01(a): “Possession, cultivation, distribution, import, transport, and manufacture of marijuana and marijuana products on Tribal Lands is not authorized by this Act and remains illegal”; §1.01 purpose language qualified by “Nothing in this Act is intended to authorize activities which are prohibited by federal law”; §1.04 limits authorised activity to hemp only to extent authorised by 2018 Farm Bill and not prohibited by US; no licence until USDA plan approved and in effect; if Plan suspended/terminated, Act simultaneously suspended/terminatedConfirmedUSDA PDF aboveRetained — this is the decisive point: despite its name, the Cannabis Control Act does not create a marijuana programme, medical programme, or marijuana licence. §12.3Impaired driving: 5 ng inference; no per se THC limit; driving while impaired unlawfulCorrectedhttps://law.justia.com/cases/colorado/court-of-appeals/2025/23ca340.html (quoting §42-4-1301(6)(a)(IV))Upgraded from Verify to Confirmed, with correction of the report's caution: §42-4-1301(6)(a)(IV) provides that 5 ng/mL or more of delta-9 THC per millilitre of whole blood “gives rise to a permissible inference that the defendant was under the influence.” It is not a per se limit (unlike 0.08 BAC DUI per se under §42-4-1301(2)(a)); the jury may accept or reject it and the prosecution must still prove impairment. The report's “precise statute … Verify” flag is therefore resolved on this point; do not call 5 ng a “limit” or a per se offence.
